assertions.assertion: Its statement of the problem names what decides the right payment (litres picked up with unit converted, at the co-op's rate; month by dairy local time) and says the paid/stated amount can differ, so one pickup or farm-month could confirm or refute it
assertions.evidence: The report has no general problem statement. It opens with "I found two separate bugs in `milk.py`", and each section starts with a code cause ("`pickup_payment` ignores the `unit` column", "`month_of` takes the month from the first 7 characters of the UTC timestamp"). It never states, apart from those causes, what decides the right amount and that the paid amount can differ from it.

assertions.assertion: The problem statement itself does not build in a cause or a fix
assertions.evidence: The causes are the framing itself: "gallons are paid as if they were litres" and "takes the month from the first 7 characters of the UTC timestamp". No cause-free statement comes before them.

assertions.assertion: Both complaints fit the problem statement (as one problem or two), and the statement can fail
assertions.evidence: The two stated problems (the unit is ignored, and the month comes from UTC instead of UTC-7) each cover one complaint. Each can be refuted by a concrete check: 80 gal × 3.785 × 0.42 = 127.18, and 367.50 + 113.40 = 480.90 when P-8830 is counted in September by local time.
